title: Prime membership for a finite free module after localization
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $F=R^{n}$ a finite free $R$-module, $s=(s_1,\dots,s_n)\in F$, and $\mathfrak p\subset R$ a prime ideal. Put $S=R\setminus\mathfrak p$ and $F_{\mathfrak p}=S^{-1}F$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], with canonical map $F\to F_{\mathfrak p}$; write $R_{\mathfrak p}=S^{-1}R$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Then $s/1\in\mathfrak pF_{\mathfrak p}$ if and only if $s\in\mathfrak pF$. Equivalently, for each coordinate, $s_i/1\in\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ if and only if $s_i\in\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Algebra, Definition Tag 00CO and the localization-at-a-prime construction; the coordinate calculation underlying Lemma Tag 00NX (lemma-finite-projective)

proof.text: Write $F=R^n$ with coordinate projections. By the definition of localization of a module [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] and coordinatewise scalar multiplication, a vector belongs to $\mathfrak pF_{\mathfrak p}$ exactly when each coordinate belongs to $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$; the canonical map sends the $i$-th coordinate $s_i$ to $s_i/1$. For a coordinate $a$, membership $a/1\in\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ means that some denominator $u\notin\mathfrak p$ satisfies $ua\in\mathfrak p$; primality of $\mathfrak p$ then gives $a\in\mathfrak p$, and the converse is immediate by taking $u=1$. Thus $s/1\in\mathfrak pF_{\mathfrak p}$ if and only if every $s_i\in\mathfrak p$, which is equivalent to $s\in\mathfrak pF$ by the coordinate description of the submodule $\mathfrak pR^n$.
